The '''2022 New Zealand Men's National League''' was the second scheduled season of the [[New Zealand National League|National League]] since its restructuring in 2021; the [[2021 New Zealand National League|2021]] National League was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand|COVID-19 pandemic]] in northern regions.<ref name="NZF-021121">{{cite web |title=National League Championship cancelled, new interregional competition announced and Chatham Cup moved to 2022 |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/109383 |website=New Zealand Football}}</ref> 32 clubs competed in the competition, with four qualifying from the [[Northern League (New Zealand)|Northern League]], three qualifying from the [[Central League (New Zealand)|Central League]] and two qualifying from the [[Southern League (New Zealand)|Southern League]] for the National Championship phase.<ref name="phxchamps"/><ref name="NLSystem">{{cite web |title=New National League system |url=https://www.sporty.co.nz/asset/downloadasset?id=3da9f0fa-187f-406d-8e40-e5a936662fcc |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=3 April 2021}}</ref>
Each team could field a maximum of four foreign players as well as one additional foreign player who has [[Oceania Football Confederation]] nationality.<ref name="breach">{{cite web |title=Two National League clubs found to have breached foreign player regulations |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/102667 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=23 April 2021 |archive-date=23 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423021812/https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/102667 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Each team also had to field at least two players aged 20 or under in the starting eleven.<ref name="under20s">{{cite web |title=Youth leads the way in new National League |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/102240 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=23 April 2021 |archive-date=23 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423021913/https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/102240 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

This season the [[Wellington Phoenix FC Reserves|Wellington Phoenix Reserves]] replaced [[Lower Hutt City AFC|Lower Hutt City]] and was allowed to play in the Central League though they still had an automatic entry into the  Championship phase.<ref name="fixtures"/><ref name="phxchamps"/> The Southern League also increased by two teams to have ten, adding three new sides to the league.<ref name="fixtures"/>

====Northern League teams====
Twelve teams are competing in the league – the top ten teams from the previous season and the two teams promoted from the 2021 [[NRFL Division 1]]. The promoted teams are [[Waiheke United AFC|Waiheke United]] and [[Takapuna AFC|Takapuna]]. This is both Waiheke's and Takapuna's first season in the Northern League.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.northernregionfootball.org.nz/newsarticle/107997|title=Northern League and LOTTO NRFL results confirmed|website=Northern Region Football|access-date=7 February 2022|archive-date=26 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126122643/https://www.northernregionfootball.org.nz/newsarticle/107997|url-status=dead}}</ref> They replaced [[Northern Rovers]] and [[West Coast Rangers]] (both teams relegated after their debut seasons in the Northern League).

==== Central League teams ====
Ten teams are competing in the league – the top nine teams from the previous season and the one team promoted from the 2021 play-off between the winners of the [[Central Federation League]] and the [[Capital Premier (New Zealand)|Capital Premier]]. The winner of the play-off was [[Havelock North Wanderers]]. This is their first season in the Central League, since New Zealand football’s restructuring in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/HNW_AFC/status/1446695727011225608?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Eembeddedtimeline%7Ctwterm%5Eprofile%3Ahnw_afc%7Ctwgr%5EeyJ0ZndfZXhwZXJpbWVudHNfY29va2llX2V4cGlyYXRpb24iOnsiYnVja2V0IjoxMjA5NjAwLCJ2ZXJzaW9uIjpudWxsfSwidGZ3X2hvcml6b25fdHdlZXRfZW1iZWRfOTU1NSI6eyJidWNrZXQiOiJodGUiLCJ2ZXJzaW9uIjpudWxsfSwidGZ3X3NwYWNlX2NhcmQiOnsiYnVja2V0Ijoib2ZmIiwidmVyc2lvbiI6bnVsbH19%7Ctwcon%5Etimelinechrome&ref_url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.hnwafc.org.nz%2F|title=SMELLS LIKE PROMOTION!|website=@HNW_AFC|access-date=7 February 2022}}</ref> They replaced [[Wainuiomata AFC|Wainuiomata]] (relegated to the Capital Premier League). [[Wairarapa United]] was entered as one of the originally 10 teams to play the 2022 season but withdrew with just two weeks to go before the start of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wairarapa United withdraw from Central League division for 2022 |url=http://www.wairarapaunited.co.nz/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/WUFC-PR-16-March-2022-1.pdf |website=Wairarapa United |access-date=16 March 2022}}</ref> They were replaced by [[Wellington United]] who had originally missed out on promotion to Havelock North Wanderers.<ref name="Update">{{cite web |title=Update to the 2022 Central League |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/113450 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=16 March 2022}}</ref> [[Lower Hutt City AFC|Lower Hutt City]] was also replaced by [[Wellington Phoenix FC Reserves|Wellington Phoenix Reserves]] for the Central League games.

==== Southern League teams ====
Ten teams are competing in the league, two more than in the previous season. The top five Mainland teams and two FootballSouth teams remain from the previous season, and are joined by two teams promoted from the 2021 [[Mainland Premier League]] and one team promoted from the 2021 [[FootballSouth Premier League]]. The promoted teams from [[Mainland Football|Mainland]] are [[Ferrymead Bays]] and [[Nomads United]], and the promoted team from FootballSouth is [[Mosgiel AFC|Mosgiel]]. This is all three teams' first season in the Southern League.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mainlandfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/106946|title=Bays Book Southern League Spot For Next Season|website=Mainland Football|access-date=7 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.footballsouth.co.nz/newsarticle/110710|title=National League & ODT Men’s Southern Premiership update|website=Football South|access-date=7 February 2022}}</ref> They replaced [[Otago University AFC|Otago University]] (relegated after the debut season of the Southern League).<ref name="fixtures">{{cite web |title=Fixtures released for Northern, Central and Southern League 2022 |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/112930 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=4 March 2022}}</ref>
